# Reproducible cloud changes across environments

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `azure-operations-iac` · **Azure & Cloud Architecture** · Catalog level: architect

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S05-Q027](#S05-Q027)

<p>How would you manage configuration across development, staging and production while promoting the same application artifact without rebuilding its code?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Design a cloud environment change that can be reproduced, checked and operated within explicit capacity and cost limits.</p>

<ul>
<li>Trace an infrastructure definition from review to the resulting resources.</li>
<li>Promote one application artifact with controlled environment configuration.</li>
<li>Choose a scaling policy from workload evidence and state when it should change.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

- [Choose cloud services from the workload](azure-service-selection.md)

<p>An environment definition describes what should exist; configuration determines how the artifact uses it; scaling controls capacity as demand changes. Follow that chain to explain what is reviewed, what differs between environments and what must be observed after deployment.</p>

### S05-Q026 · Mechanism

<p>What does infrastructure as code change about provisioning and updating an environment?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q026](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q026)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q026](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q026)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain infrastructure-as-code concepts and deployment templates.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Infrastructure as code represents infrastructure changes in reviewable definitions. Explain how a deployment template moves from a proposed change to observable infrastructure.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Describe infrastructure change as a controlled and verifiable lifecycle.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name the tooling and cloud provider; distinguish infrastructure definitions, environment parameters and application releases. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces review, planned changes and verification for a concrete resource update.</li>
<li>Explains how unexpected environment differences would be detected and investigated.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Equating a checked-in template with proof that the deployed environment matches it.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you handle a manual resource change that is absent from the definitions?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q027"></a>

### S05-Q027 · Application

<a id="S05-Q038"></a>

<p>How would you manage configuration across development, staging and production while promoting the same application artifact without rebuilding its code?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q027](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q027) · [S05-Q038](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q038)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q027](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q027)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How should environment-specific configuration be managed?

</div>

**[S05-Q038](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q038)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How should configuration differ across development, staging and production without rebuilding application code?

</div>

**Why these source prompts share a canonical question:** Same environment configuration contract; retain cloud deployment and immutable container/artifact contexts.

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Cover both cloud deployment parameters and the configuration used by a container or other application artifact. Explain ownership and verification of the environment differences.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Design a configuration contract that preserves artifact identity across environments.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Distinguish build inputs, runtime settings and secrets; clarify whether changes require a restart or may be applied during execution.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Maps each environment difference to a controlled configuration owner and delivery point.</li>
<li>Checks artifact identity and detects a missing or incorrectly targeted setting.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Rebuilding environment-specific application code while claiming to test and promote the same artifact.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you diagnose staging passing while production uses a different database endpoint?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q025"></a>

### S05-Q025 · Trade-offs

<p>How would you choose an autoscaling policy while balancing reliability, response time and cost?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q025](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q025)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q025](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q025)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Discuss autoscaling, reliability and cost trade-offs.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Autoscaling changes capacity according to a policy. Explain the workload signal, the intended outcome and the limit that could make more capacity ineffective.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Make a capacity decision with explicit budgets and a verification plan.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Clarify load shape, bottleneck, startup time and service limits; identify the cloud service and deployment model. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connects a scaling trigger and limit to the workload’s observable behavior.</li>
<li>Designs a load or failure check and states which evidence would justify changing the policy.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming adding replicas fixes every bottleneck or that one utilization threshold fits every workload.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would you check if replicas increase but tail latency does not improve?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>An ASP.NET Core service passes staging, but production uses a different database endpoint and its replicas keep increasing during peak traffic. Produce a change plan showing artifact identity, infrastructure and configuration ownership, scaling hypotheses, validation and a safe recovery decision. Establish the actual Azure service and policy before making provider-specific claims.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Defines infrastructure as code, environment configuration and autoscaling, with a concrete purpose for each.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Connects definitions, artifact promotion and measured capacity into one change plan; defends limits and a representative validation path.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>A checked-in template or utilization screenshot alone does not show deployed configuration, artifact identity or the effect of a scaling change.</p>
